messages:
alex: Heads-up — saw a weird perf inversion on seq=1024 between H100 and A100 when using the new vectorized attention microkernel. On H100 we're ~18% slower than A100 for the 1K window. Anyone seen this?

maria: Which variant — v2 tiled or the scalar fallback?

alex: v2 tiled (tile=128, qk packed). We do runtime sm capability detection but maybe it's mis-classifying H100 vs L4 emulation. Reproducer: `bin/microbench --model=gpt2 --seq=1024 --kernel=attn_v2_tiled` on h100-32g-ptx-ml-07.

sam: Could be DPX vs DPAS behavior. H100 benefits from DPX/TF32 paths, our inner loop uses custom FMAs that don't map to DPX so the HW path is slower. What flags are we gating on?

alex: Right now runtime checks `sm_caps & SM_CAP_DP4A` and `SM_CAP_WMMA` then picks the tiled kernel. H100 exposes DPX-style flags (dp_x) which we try to map, but mapping is messy.

rachel: Telemetry from that host shows flags [wmma, dpasx, shuffle64]. Our mapping reduces that to {wmma, dpa} and the kernel predicate expects {wmma, dp_x}. If mapping misses dp_x we pick suboptimal kernel.

maria: L4 is another dimension — it lacks tensor cores and some fp16 vector instrs, but our tiled kernel still executes with vector intrinsics and hits alignment penalties. We should tighten capability checks so kernels only run when device truly supports required ops.

alex: Proposal: replace ad-hoc booleans with a capability vector string, e.g. `sm:wmma:dp_x:fp16-vec:shuffle64`. Each kernel declares a required-cap set and we check set inclusion.

sam: Implementation: compute a bitmask once per device UUID at process start, cache it. Keep checks cheap in hot path. Recompute if driver reloads.

maria: Also add a tiny startup microprobe for attention kernels — a 100ms run that validates chosen kernel perf and reports ops/sec. If regression, fall back.

rachel: +1. We'll add metrics to Console: `chosen_kernel`, `probe_latency_us`, `probe_ops_per_sec`, `fallback_reason`.

probe-bot: REPORT: host=h100-32g-ptx-ml-07 kernel=attn_v2_tiled perf=-18% vs baseline attn_v1_scalar. Suggested action: run microprobe and mark host for manual review.

alex: OK plan summary: (1) capability vector schema & stable encoding; (2) cached device-cap bitmask keyed by UUID; (3) startup microprobe + telemetry; (4) kernel manifest with `required_caps` and estimated throughput; (5) rollout: canary opt-in then auto rollout with regression guardrails.

maria: Edge cases: multi-GPU machines with mixed SM families — route requests per-device and avoid assuming uniform performance. Also detect driver versions and known-bug workarounds.

sam: Add note: quantized int8 kernels rely on int8 dotpack ops that L4 emulates slowly. Mark those kernels with `requires:int8-dot` so runtime won't pick them on L4.

alex: I'll draft an RFC and perf harness. Who can pair on perf tests + telemetry? @rachel?

rachel: Can do. I'll add the telemetry and create the Console panels. Also add ops-regression alert when chosen_kernel causes >10% p50 latency regression for 5m.

maria: I'll help define capability schema and mapping table. Use a stable string encoding (no random ordering) so queries don't break.

sam: I'll implement the microbench and cached-cap bitmask PR.

alex: Thanks all. Action items: RFC draft by EOD Friday; PRs next week. :thumbsup:

probe-bot: deploybot: canary test enqueued on h100-32g-ptx-ml-07 (job id 78902).

alex: Great — let us know results and we can iterate.
